I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so at the start of the growing season I will stick with the pattern that fits my land, water, and labor best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the safest and most familiar double-cropping system for me. I am 45, I have primary schooling, and I rely on methods that are practical, proven, and easy to manage on time. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence, better disease resistance, and higher yield than old saved seed. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer moderate and split nitrogen so the crop does not grow too soft. I will irrigate a few key times because water matters a lot here, but I will not waste it. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient and suits my field conditions. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize, use hybrid seed, apply enough nitrogen for strong growth, and irrigate when the crop most needs it. I will spray pesticides only as needed for common weeds, insects, and diseases, because too many sprays cost money and are hard on the crop. My goal is stable grain output and manageable field work through the whole year.
